instructor:

Even with his negative traits as a teacher, I would definitely choose him again as my teacher.  

Negative: He is STRICT. He always used all the spare hours for the whole semester. It is absolutely not allowed to look at your phone and if you get caught, he loudly warns you by your name. If you arrive at the class like 2-3 minutes late, you need to write your name on a piece of paper and if your name is written 3 times, you lose participation points. You need to actively participate to almost all the classes. There is also a strict attendance policy. It is also sometimes hard to listen to him because it is easy to lost his track of thought. Lastly, even with his excellent teaching skills, I believe his expectations are too high on the exams and you sometimes get lower than you expected.

I think he's a very knowledgeable and accomplished professor; I've learned a lot from him. I think the TAship and articles are excellent choices that keep you engaged and focused in class. You get used to reading articles, and they form the basis for much of what he explains in class, independent of the slides. If you want to get a good grade in this course, you need to read the articles beforehand and come to class prepared, and you need to take notes on everything Jed hoca says without missing a single class. In this respect, it's actually a bit challenging because staying fully focused, especially in such an intense year, is difficult, but that's why they make us do TAship – so everyone can fill in any important gaps in their knowledge from the videos. TAship, on the one hand, definitely contributes to a much more comprehensive understanding of the subject for those who are assistants. As I said, it's a bit intense and tiring, but since all third-year psychology courses have very intensive content, this activity doesn't really stand out too much among the others. Listening to Jed hoca is important because he explains the lessons very intensively, especially in terms of language. In this context, I might say that there's a difficult aspect, particularly reflected in exam results, for non-native speakers, regardless of how good their English is. Each week, he provides clear definitions and vocabulary explanations for the topics covered, and sometimes, no matter how much you study, it can be difficult to write the exact words Jed hoca uses in class, inevitably leading to a loss of points. It could be a little more flexible, but this is just a small suggestion; maybe I'm wrong.

Jed Hoca is my favourite instructor in Bilkent, and I always learn so much in his courses. He is an excellent teacher and he is really good at transferring his knowledge to his students. The way he makes his students think critically and analytically about the topics covered in class is unmatched. He is also a very approachable person and open to all sorts of feedback from students. It is also worth mentioning that he tries his best to always be fair to his students, and equity between his students is an important issue for him. I have taken 3 courses from him prior to this, I got As in all of them; they were not easy courses, but I still enjoyed taking them from Jed Hoca very much. HOWEVER, this specific course turned into a nightmare for me, and my classmates (as I learned after I talked to them about this issue), for various reasons. The biggest issue is that this is a 3 credit course, like every single department elective that we are offered, yet the workload is immense. Firstly, the topics covered in this course are really advanced, and no prerequisite in the psychology department could make up for this. You are expected to read 30+ pages of advanced readings that are in no way introductory level, every week before coming to class to teach yourself the topic, as the classes are not lecture style. Reading them takes so much time since the language used in them is so technical and heavy, and I almost exclusively failed to truly understand them every week, but you are expected to be able to do that for 3 reasons. You are expected to (1) actively participate in class discussions about that topic (which was super hard for me, because I really don’t like participating in a discussion if I don’t have anything worthy to add--- (CONTINUED IN NEXT QUESTION)
course: (CONTINUED) --which was mostly the case for this class due to the topics being really advanced), (2) write a thought paper/ discussion comment (about 500-1000 words) every single week BEFORE class (so you better teach understand that reading on your own), and (3) the instructor will not explicitly teach you that topic in a lecture style, the class will just consist of a deep discussion about that topic. This becomes super frustrating after a while since you need to read long theoretical articles that you barely even understand every week, then write about it every week, on top of reading the things that your classmates have written about it in the forum. If this wasn’t frustrating enough, the midterm for this class was writing not one, but TWO 2500 word essays, which is roughly around 20 pages. DURING YOUR MIDTERM WEEK, so best of luck to my fellow students who are taking any other courses other than this at the same time :) Another graded activity that you have to complete is being the discussion leader for a week, which roughly translates into having a deep understanding of that week’s topic on your own, reading every single thought paper and forum post that is posted by your classmates that week (about 1000 words each), extracting questions from every single one of them to direct to class, preparing powerpoint slides to present to the class, and preparing a separate handout which is a summary of that week’s reading with definitions, then doing a presentation for the whole duration of that week’s class (3 hours). On top of all this, there is still the final exam, which consists of a proposal (1000 words) that should include a bibliography of 6-10 articles about your topic, and the final essay (3500 words). It is absolutely ridiculous that this course has the same amount of credits as the other courses that I am taking at the same time. The amount of work for this course is more than the 6 other courses I am currently taking COMBINED.
